title: Liverpool’s slave-trade past, read in its streets and stones
episode: Liverpool & Slavery: Uncovering a Brutal History
description: Liverpool ships carried well over a million enslaved Africans across the Atlantic. Behind the Town Hall, the merchants’ square of Exchange Flags holds the 1813 Nelson monument, whose four chained captives are often read as an echo of that trade.

title: A museum on the dock where slaving ships were fitted out
place: International Slavery Museum, Royal Albert Dock
description: An introduction to the International Slavery Museum, opened in 2007 inside the Merseyside Maritime Museum on the Royal Albert Dock. It covers the transatlantic slave trade, Liverpool’s central part in it, and racism and resistance since.

title: A future king inspects the tunnel under the Mersey
episode: ROYAL: Prince of Wales visits Mersey Tunnel (1930)
description: British Pathé newsreel of the Prince of Wales, later Edward VIII, touring the Queensway road tunnel under the River Mersey during construction. Opened in 1934, it was then the world’s longest underwater road tunnel; its city entrance is at Old Haymarket.

title: Twenty-two-year-old architect, seventy-four years of building
description: Architect Giles Gilbert Scott won the competition for Liverpool’s Anglican cathedral in 1903, aged 22. Building ran from 1904 to 1978, long after his death, producing Britain’s largest cathedral on a sandstone ridge above the city.

title: Concrete, clock towers and two copper birds
episode: Liverpool’s Royal Liver Building: The Architecture that Inspired the Beatles
description: Walter Aubrey Thomas’s Royal Liver Building, finished in 1911 for an insurance society, was among the first big reinforced-concrete buildings. Its two Liver Birds, the city’s mythical emblem, watch over the Pier Head waterfront and the river.

title: Europe’s oldest Chinese community, filmed in 1981
description: Archive footage of Liverpool’s Chinatown, home to Europe’s oldest Chinese community, which grew from seamen of the Blue Funnel shipping line in the late 1800s. Its centre is Nelson Street, now marked by a large ornamental arch built in 2000.

title: The Chinese seamen shipped out of Liverpool after the war
episode: My Stolen Chinese Father: Victims Of UK's Racist Past
place: Chinese seamen memorial plaque, Pier Head
description: In 1945–46 the British government quietly deported hundreds of Chinese merchant seamen from Liverpool, many leaving wives and children who never learned why. A plaque on the Pier Head waterfront has remembered them since 2006.

title: Granada’s current-affairs cameras return to Toxteth
description: Granada TV’s World in Action returns to Toxteth, the inner-city district where July 1981 saw days of rioting between young people and police after an arrest. Upper Parliament Street, where the Rialto ballroom burned, was at its centre.

title: Toxteth’s 1981 riots, told from inside the neighbourhood
description: The 1981 Toxteth riots as seen from L8, the postcode of Liverpool’s long-established Black community. Granby Street, the district’s old shopping street, was at the heart of the area worst affected by the unrest and the neglect that followed.
